channel.title: Jayesh Suryavanshi · Writing
channel.description: Technical studies and field notes on machine learning, LLM agents, and the models I take apart.

item.title: The browser is a peripheral
item.description: Claude Code can drive Chrome. The documentation covers what it can do and stays quiet on how. Reading the shipped binary, the extension bundle and the MCP server's own session logs turns up five hops, two transports, a coordinate frame that disagrees with its own declared scale, and one surprise about where your page text goes.

item.title: The empty classroom
item.description: A deep learning professor at IISc Bangalore put down his prepared lecture and spent the hour asking his students why they still come to class. He is also the one automating the answer away: no more research assistants, his own learning moved to an LLM, and a skill on his company's marketplace built to teach in his voice.

item.title: The unmapped majority
item.description: Most geotagged-social pipelines quietly map the 1-2% of posts that carry exact coordinates and call it 'the geography.' Count the coverage first and a different picture appears. A worked example with GeoSocialX: on a realistic 5,000-post city pull, 84% have no location, place-resolution recovers 10x more than exact coordinates alone, and the honest move is to report the hole.

item.title: Informative but subsumed
item.description: What news text really adds to unrest forecasting, measured properly: 336M events, 55 countries, leakage-controlled out-of-time backtests, and a signal ladder from tone counts to neural headline embeddings. The semantics of news are already in the event record.

item.title: The closed frontier, mid-2026
item.description: GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8 & Fable 5, and Grok 4.5, who actually holds the crown at the closed frontier, and why nobody holds all of it. A benchmark-checked, adversarially fact-checked field guide.

item.title: Inkling, up close
item.description: A close technical read of Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling: a 975B-parameter open-weights multimodal MoE. What's actually new in the architecture, where it really lands on benchmarks, the interaction-models system it was built for, and how to fine-tune it on Tinker.

item.title: The open-weights frontier, mid-2026
item.description: Five open-weights models (Inkling, GLM 5.2, Kimi K2.7, DeepSeek V4, and Nemotron 3 Ultra) and who actually wins what. A benchmark-checked field guide to the state of open models in mid-2026.
